exposure: intrapartum CS for failure to progress
cohort: Women who gave birth in 2015 (pre-intervention) and 2018 (post-intervention) at a university-affiliated teaching hospital in the Slovak Republic
finding: Implementation of a multifaceted quality-improvement intervention led to a significant reduction in the rate of cesarean section without affecting the rate of perinatal mortality.
mod_finding: The QI intervention led to a reduction in both elective CS for non-obstetric reasons and intrapartum CS for failure to progress, as well as an increase in the number of vaginal births after CS.
